articles.title: ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot
articles.summary: After battling it out in the arena in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and leading the latest “Karate Kid” installment, Ben Wang is circling another major franchise: Marvel Studios’ “X-Men” reboot. Wang is in negotiations to play Bobby Drake, aka Iceman, who was one of the founding X-Men.
body: If the deal closes, Wang would join a sprawling cast that features Sadie Sink (as Jean Grey), Kit Connor (as Cyclops), Samara Weaving (as Emma Frost), Inde Navarrette (as Rogue), Maya Boyd (as Storm), Asa Germann (as Angel), Christopher Abbott (as Professor Charles Xavier) and Adam Driver (as Mr. Sinister).

Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige revealed the new “X-Men” cast at the D23 convention in August, after Sink’s Jean Grey debuted in the blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The upcoming movie reboots the mutant team for the first time since the 2019 Fox film “X-Men: Dark Phoenix” and for their first outing under the Marvel Studios umbrella. Jake Schreier, who oversaw last year’s “Thunderbolts,” is directing the film from a script by Lee Sung Jin and Joanna Calo. “X-Men” is set for release on May 5, 2028.

articles.title: Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story
articles.summary: Jessica Alba was nine months pregnant, stressed out of her mind and battling a bad allergic reaction to laundry detergent when she decided to launch her first business.
body: Alba’s determination to launch a company that used safe and healthy chemicals in skin care and cleaning products was realized after the birth of her daughter. The Honest Company made its retail debut in 2012 with a handful of products. Nine years later, the company had a successful IPO, making Alba one of the youngest and one of the few Latinas to take a company public.

In the conversation with Kelso, moderated by Cynthia Littleton, Variety ’s co-Editor in Chief, Alba recalled the hard work of getting the company off the ground. She was ahead of the curve in recognizing that her name recognition could be harnessed to create awareness for her brand.
The learning curve was steep, Alba admitted to the invitation-only crowd of small business owners, entrepreneurs and business influencers.

articles.title: Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses
articles.summary: Meta is helping bring Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” to 3D screens — and its upcoming VR glasses. The studio and tech company have partnered to convert the film to 3D ahead of its Nov. 20 release, marking Meta’s first time working with a studio on such a conversion.
body: Meta is helping bring Lionsgate ‘s “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” to 3D screens — and its upcoming VR glasses.

The 3D version will also be available on Meta’s new $1,299 VR glasses when they release in the spring. Jim Packer, Lionsgate’s chief revenue officer, called the collaboration a “compelling example of how technology can transform existing formats to create fresh, new experiences” in a statement.

“As we continue to explore new ways for audiences to experience ‘The Hunger Games,’ we’re thrilled to partner with Meta on this first-of-its-kind collaboration,” Packer said. “[Director] Francis Lawrence has created an incredible 3D experience for ‘ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,’ and we’re excited for audiences to experience it in theaters and then on Meta VR Glasses.”

Lawrence said the 3D adaptation gave the team another way to let audiences experience the journey of Joseph Zada’s Haymitch Abernathy, a younger version of the character originated by Woody Harrelson, whom audiences follow through the 50th edition of the Hunger Games.

articles.title: One in a Million review – deeply moving film about displacement, freedom and the upheaval of starting again
articles.summary: Following a Syrian mother and daughter over a decade, Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes capture a family transformed. There’s a startling moment in this BBC refugee documentary when Syrian mother Nisreen – in the apparently miserable situation of hiking across the Balkans towards Germany, four kids in…
body: Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes’ superb, forthright and highly moving film bypasses the usual refugee dichotomies, that they’re either external threats or history’s victims. Instead of flat abstractions, we get the knotty reality. Focused over a 10-year period from 2015 to 2025 principally on Nisreen’s eldest daughter Israa, it presents an intimate chronicle of how geographical displacement and cultural dislocation reshape families and lives from the inside.

It’s a wrenchingly immediate demonstration of the neglected flip side to discussions of how immigrants alter host countries – and how the immigrants themselves are also changed in the process. Through the young man who becomes her husband, Israa slowly comes to a rapprochement with her Syrian and Muslim identity – and finally makes an Ithacan return to Aleppo. But the damage is harder to repair for once-respected shawarma chef Tarek, who in his own moment of truth admits he made his family pay for his loss of status. As his daughter says at the start: “War is not as hard as what comes after.”

articles.title: ‘Sad lost souls’: Taika Waititi lambasts critics after Klara and the Sun box-office disaster
articles.summary: The Jojo Rabbit director blamed the dismal numbers for his film of Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel on ‘obsolete’ reviewers’ notices, adding that he works ‘for the people’ – whose Rotten Tomatoes ratings are much higher.
body: Taika Waititi has launched a furious broadside at “critics” following the disastrous commercial performance of Klara and the Sun, his new film adapted from a Kazuo Ishiguro novel.
In a post on social media, Waititi wrote: “This Halloween, let’s spare a thought for those sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists, and thus settled, and became critics.”
He added: “The same people who also hated Jojo Rabbit … Irrelevant. Out of touch. Obsolete. In the bin.”

Pointing to the disparity of the film’s audience and critics’ score on review aggregator site Rotten Tomatoes, which currently stands at 74% for the former and 26% (from 90 reviews) for the latter, Waititi also wrote: “I haven’t read a review of anything aimed at me or my peers in almost 15 years. But I do listen to the people.”

articles.title: Blockhead review – struggling novelist embraces his inner monster in comic thriller of literary machismo
articles.summary: Writer-director Matt Harlock looks into ego and insecurity in a smart film about a BritLit bad boy who goes down a grisly road. This has nothing to do with Ian Dury; rather, it is a brisk, effective British indie thriller informed by the legend of Robert Louis Stevenson wrestling his shadow self…
body: No prizes, then, for guessing which David Fincher film provides the template here. Typing to a soundtrack of his own best reviews (“The world needs to hear your story”), an emboldened Will is soon exploring grislier avenues, including home invasion and murder, while his increasingly unhinged rants to creative-writing students attract a rapt protege. Evoking a world where publishers push books with unequivocally positive pull quotes like “confrontational” and “dangerous”, Harlock is taking a red pencil to hackneyed notions of bad-boy writers. There is, he posits, only so much muscle one can wield while hunched over a laptop.

articles.title: Suitcase Richard Burton sent Elizabeth Taylor's clothes to sister in up for auction
articles.summary: The Welsh film star sent his then-wife and actress Elizabeth Taylor's unwanted clothes to his sister.
body: A suitcase once containing Elizabeth Taylor's unwanted clothes which was shipped by Richard Burton to his sister suggesting to give them to "old colliers" is up for auction.
Burton, from Pontrhydyfen in Neath Port Talbot, wrote to his sister Hilda from Switzerland saying "don't pass out but this is from me" as he sent her the clothes in 1971.
Burton was married five times, twice to Taylor with whom he starred in 11 films. Their relationship was born from an affair while filming Cleopatra together in the 1960s.
The suitcase the clothes contained and the letter Burton sent his sister are among a stash of Welsh memorabilia up for auction on Thursday.

articles.title: ‘We both know how we feel about death and dying’: Rhys Ifans and Laura Linney on their brutally honest Parkinson’s drama
articles.summary: Written by Vicar of Dibley co-creator Paul Mayhew-Archer, who has the disease, Onwards and Sideways sees the actors play a couple who bond over their diagnoses – a devastating subject but laced with humour too, they say.
body: A head of production on their first job together, Rhys Ifans and Laura Linney didn’t undergo the standard “chemistry read” to make sure they got on. Which is remarkable, given what their characters would have to do to each other in Onwards and Sideways.

In the Norfolk-set BBC film directed by John Madden (Shakespeare in Love), Ifans would have to nearly throttle Linney while in the grip of night terrors, she’d have to collapse in his arms in a weeping mess having bankrupted herself with a gambling addiction; both situations arising from the neurological condition afflicting their characters: Parkinson’s disease.

But despite being thrown into the deep end in this hugely emotional, often hilarious film, both actors acknowledge an immediate feeling of safety around each other as they embarked on a project that would require them to strip themselves bare. “It’s odd,” says Ifans, “you learn so much about each other so quickly. I couldn’t tell you what kind of car Laura drives. What her home looks like. But we both know how we feel about death and dying.”

articles.title: Channel 4 documentary and journalists 'poisoned the well' against Russell Brand, court hears
articles.summary: Brand's defence barrister told jurors that Brand "had an immense amount of sex", but that "none of it was unlawful".
body: Journalists "poisoned the well of justice" by prompting complainants to come forward and make criminal allegations against Russell Brand, jurors have heard.

In his closing speech on Monday, Ian Winter KC, Brand's defence barrister, said a Channel 4 documentary and stories in the Times and Sunday Times that made allegations about Brand in 2023 "caused people who had not previously considered for it to be appropriate to bring criminal allegations against him, to do so, and very many years after."
Brand faces seven counts; three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
On Monday at Southwark Crown Court, Winter told jurors that "living a highly promiscuous life is entirely lawful".

articles.title: 'I decided I was going to be Taylor Swift' - singer goes from busking to The Voice UK winner
articles.summary: Cate McHugh has gone from busking on the streets of Cardiff to winner of The Voice UK.
body: The winner of the Voice UK says she decided "I was going to be Taylor Swift" as a teenager after being given a guitar, before busking on the streets of Cardiff.
Welsh singer Cate McHugh was crowned the winner of the show on Saturday, after being mentored by "the legend that is Sir Tom Jones".
McHugh, from Llantwit Major, in the Vale of Glamorgan, said Sir Tom was so warm and supportive that it felt "as if you've known him for years".
One of the standout pieces of advice he gave to her early on was to focus on the story being told in the song, she explained.
